grade.basis: Independent whole-work inspection of the publisher watermarked perusal, notation pages 1–10 (cached images 3–12). Cello 1 moves from low bass-clef melody to an exposed upper-register treble-clef version, with sustained notes reaching above the treble staff; this requires secure upper-position/thumb-position intonation and controlled singing tone. Cello 2 also reads treble clef, cello 4 later climbs well above the bass staff, and cello 6 has recurring widely spaced two-note pizzicato/arco sonorities. The rhythmic vocabulary is overwhelmingly long values, ties and occasional duplets, without rapid passagework, difficult rapid string crossings or virtuoso bowing. Long sustained chromatically inflected lines, dynamic changes and the five-minute expressive span justify advanced instrumental control, but eight-part tuning and coordination alone do not raise the grade. Advisory estimate within approximately one level, not an exhaustive technical certification.

findings.finding: Complete public publisher perusal inspected through the final a niente and fermata: printed score pages 1–10, cached preview images 3–12. Con pietà, quarter note approximately 108, with a predominantly sustained chorale texture. Upper-register cello 1 writing appears from rehearsal 7 onward and is the principal individual technical demand; the final pages do not introduce fast figurations.
Publisher context identifies Chorale (1994) for eight cellos, approximately five minutes. The modal/chromatically inflected harmony does not support a confident simple major/minor label.
